_comment: Cases for the rules the validator and the golden-prompt grader BOTH implement.
One file, two readers: validate-skill-pack.tests.ps1 and test_grade_golden_output.py.
This exists because the two tools are one rule set written twice in two
languages, and they drifted on three rules at once without anything noticing:
the grader exempted every leading pipe, accepted any mention of _time as a
time bound, and read KQL tables a line at a time. CI was green, the mutation
harness was green, and a review bot found it. CLAUDE.md says to port these
rules rather than re-derive them, but that is a note to a human. This file is
the mechanical half: a rule that holds in one tool and not the other fails a
suite instead of surviving until someone reads both implementations.
Add a case here rather than to one suite whenever the behaviour is shared.
Both readers are dependency-free: ConvertFrom-Json ships with PowerShell and
json ships with Python, which is the constraint that rules out anything
cleverer than a flat JSON file.
_kql_tables_comment: Every table a kql block references: the leading source, plus union and join
operands and any table bound by let. The two implementations split at
different seams, so each reader normalises before comparing:
- the grader's kql_tables() filters the placeholder names itself, because
it has no registry to check them against
- the validator's Get-KqlTableReferences returns them, and the catalogue
then accepts them because it lists both as placeholder rows
Each reader subtracts 'placeholders' below, so the comparison is of the rule
and not of where each tool happens to draw the line.

kql_tables.name: a leading function call is not a table
kql_tables.why: Microsoft ships _SentinelHealth() and tells you to prefer it over the raw table.

kql_tables.name: union withsource wildcard names no table
kql_tables.why: The option must be consumed or 'withsource' itself is captured as the operand.

kql_tables.name: parenthesized union operand
kql_tables.why: KQL's commonest union form. A pattern accepting only a bare identifier read no table here.

kql_tables.name: parenthesized union operand behind an option
a union operand list wraps on a trailing comma
a bare union operand list wraps on a trailing comma
a union statement ends at a pipe outside its parentheses
kql_tables.why: Otherwise the summarize columns are read as operands.
kql_tables.query: union SigninLogs, AuditLogs | summarize count() by Alpha, Beta

kql_tables.name: downstream summarize columns are not operands
kql_tables.query:
SigninLogs
| summarize count() by Alpha, Beta
| project Gamma, Delta

kql_tables.name: join operand on the same line
join operand on the next line
kql_tables.why: How a model formats a wide join. The line-oriented scan could not see past the newline.
kql_tables.query:
SigninLogs
| join (
    AuditLogs
    | take 5
) on Id

kql_tables.name: a table bound by let
kql_tables.why: The name the let BINDS is a local, not a table, and must not be reported.

kql_tables.name: a let binding a function call contributes no table
the source is read past a let preamble
kql_tables.why: Reading line 0 only hid the real table behind the let.

kql_tables.name: a comment line is not the source

_spl_time_bound_comment: Whether a raw-event SPL block must be reported for having no time bound.
'reported' is the shared outcome, deliberately, because the two tools split
this differently: the validator returns early for a generating command while
the grader runs no check at all. Both agree on what counts as a violation,
which is the thing worth pinning.
A bound is a time PREDICATE, not a mention of _time: 'index=x | stats
latest(_time)' scans all history but contains the string. '| head' is an
accepted alternative bound. A block leading with a GENERATING command runs
unbounded on purpose and is exempt -- but '| search' is a raw-event search
wearing that syntax and is not.

spl_time_bound.name: earliest= bounds it
spl_time_bound.query:
index=windows earliest=-24h
| stats count by host

spl_time_bound.name: earliest= may sit on a later line
spl_time_bound.why: A base search wraps in real model output even though the docs write it on one line.
spl_time_bound.query:
((index=firewall sourcetype=cisco:asa) OR (index=proxy sourcetype=bluecoat:proxysg:access:kv))
earliest=-24h latest=now
| stats count by src

spl_time_bound.name: _time inside an aggregation is not a bound
spl_time_bound.why: Scans all history but contains the string '_time'. A substring test passed it.

spl_time_bound.name: _time inside an aggregation on its own line is not a bound
a generating command runs unbounded on purpose
spl_time_bound.query: | tstats count where index=windows by index, sourcetype

spl_time_bound.name: a leading-pipe search is still a raw-event search
spl_time_bound.why: '| search index=...' wears a generating command's syntax. Exempting every leading pipe skipped the check entirely.

spl_time_bound.name: a leading-pipe search with a bound is fine
